question: What fundamentally new architecture could give an AI system abilities that today's large language models fundamentally lack? Propose concrete architectural or algorithmic mechanisms - not scaling, and not incremental improvements of transformers.
crux: Each architecture's self-improvement loop needs a trustworthy correctness signal: the "realized uncertainty reduction" bids are paid on, the prediction errors that trigger patches or graph revisions, the "symbolic or learned checker", the "ground-truth-verified" error map, the regression suite and the contradiction detector. None of the answers says where that signal comes from in open-ended, real-world domains, where there is no oracle and the system would end up grading itself with the same fallible model it is trying to correct.
